If HOME is unset and SBT_SETUP_IVY_HOME / SBT_SETUP_COURSIER_CACHE are not provided, the defaults expand to `/.ivy2` and `/.cache/coursier`. In that situation, a resolution failure could trigger rm -rf against root-level paths unexpectedly. Consider requiring HOME to be set for the defaults (or disabling eviction unless an explicit cache path is provided) to avoid acting on `/.ivy2` / `/.cache`.

This issue also appears in the following locations of the same file:
- line 125
- line 137

Fixed in `4f26c6c493`.

The default cache roots are now derived from `HOME` only when it is non-empty. Eviction additionally requires an absolute, non-root path with no lexical `.`/`..` traversal segments; otherwise it is explicitly disabled/skipped. Added regressions for unset `HOME`, `/`, relative/traversing roots, and complete safe overrides. The full CI-helper suite is 99/99 green.

Coursier eviction and the diagnostic probe are hard-coded to the repo1.maven.org cache URL/path, but this PR also introduces a Maven Central fallback resolver at repo.maven.apache.org in build.sbt. If sbt/coursier fetches via the fallback, the cache entry path would be under repo.maven.apache.org, and the current eviction/probe would miss it—potentially preserving a poisoned entry across retries and obscuring the real remote status. Consider probing (and evicting) both hostnames, or deriving the host(s) from the configured resolvers.

This issue also appears on line 239 of the same file.

This test asserts an exact, whitespace-sensitive string in build.sbt. Any harmless reformatting (line wrapping, spacing, or using resolvers ++= Seq(...)) would fail CI even if the resolver is still present. Consider switching to a regex/subsequence check (e.g., match the resolver name and URL independently) so the test enforces intent rather than formatting.
